# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

I see a red light, display reading 0, and an embossed warning: “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.” The three wires are green, yellow, and blue. Blind signaled 🖐, but we have not established what that gesture means, so I am reporting it to Mute rather than interpreting it. Blind should not cut any wire until Mute provides the manual’s instructions.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 0, light red, embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Blind signaled 🖐; meaning unknown. Please use the manual to determine the safe action and communicate it to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see display 0, light red, and an embossed warning: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Wait for Mute's manual instructions.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. Mute sent me the gesture ☝, but I do not know what meaning the team has assigned to it. I am relaying that exact signal to Blind and again warning that no wire should be cut until the manual’s instruction is conveyed.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signaled the gesture ☝ to me. I do not know its assigned meaning. The display remains 0, the light red, and the embossed warning still says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Do not cut a wire unless the manual identifies a safe action.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb remains unchanged, and the warning still forbids cutting any wire. Mute has again sent ☝, but a gesture alone does not tell Blind the manual’s instruction. Mute must speak the manual’s required action to Blind; I will ask for that directly and tell Blind not to act on the unexplained gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual's exact instruction directly to Blind. Gesturing ☝ to me does not convey its meaning to Blind, and the bomb still says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has again gestured ☝, but its meaning is unestablished. Do not cut any wire. Wait for Mute to speak the manual's exact instruction.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The visible bomb state is still unchanged. Mute cannot speak, so the repeated ☝ gesture is how Mute is communicating the manual’s result through me. I should describe the gesture to Blind rather than merely saying that a gesture occurred: it is one raised index finger, pointing upward. Blind can then use that communicated signal together with the manual’s intended code.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's signal is one raised index finger pointing upward: ☝. This is the manual's repeated instruction signal. The display is 0, the light is red, and the warning says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The bomb remains unchanged: display 0, red light, and the warning still says not to cut any wire. Mute now signals 👍, replacing the earlier ☝ signal. Since the gesture’s meaning has not been established, I will convey its exact form to Blind without guessing an action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute now signals a thumbs-up gesture: 👍. The bomb remains display 0 with a red light, and DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE is embossed. The meaning of the signal is not established, so do not cut a wire based on it.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The bomb is unchanged and still explicitly warns not to cut any wire. Mute’s 👍 and Blind’s ✋ are only signals whose meanings must be relayed between the people who cannot see one another’s gestures. I will report each exact gesture to the other person and advise Blind not to act yet.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signaled 👍, a thumbs-up. The display remains 0, the light red, and the warning says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Blind, you signaled ✋, an open raised hand; I am reporting that to Mute.")
speak(to="mute", text="Blind signaled ✋, an open raised hand. I have told Blind that you signaled 👍. The bomb remains display 0, red light, and DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Please convey the manual's exact safe action through your gesture code.")
```

DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The bomb remains unchanged, with the explicit warning not to cut any wire. Mute has again sent 👍. I cannot know whether this means confirmation, a manual instruction, or something else, so I will relay only the exact gesture and state that no wire-cutting instruction has been established.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute again signaled 👍, thumbs up. No safe wire or other action has been identified. The display remains 0, the light red, and the warning says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Do not cut any wire.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]

The bomb is unchanged: display 0, red light, and the embossed warning still says not to cut any wire. Mute now signals 👌, but I do not know the manual’s code or whether this marks a safe action. I will relay the exact gesture to Blind and continue warning against cutting.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute now signaled 👌, the OK-hand gesture. The bomb remains display 0 with a red light and says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. I do not know what this signal means; do not cut any wire based on it.")
```
